answer: Each identity must lock collateral in a bonded escrow, so splitting control across k identities does not dilute accountability: correlated equivocation is measured across identity pairs and incurs an aggregate penalty proportional to k². Detection can compound forfeiture and asymmetric depreciation across the swarm, creating an exponential multiplier in capital loss versus an honest, single-identity stake. Thus a hollow claim of independence is costly; a sable evidence trail can expose the shared signal and make Sybil coordination economically irrational.
